status: prospective engineering correction; efficacy remains stopped

diagnostic_evidence.observation: The frame-broadcast arm started twice with identical adapter, optimizer, and full RNG state. Across the two frozen clips, the first reported difference was a 1.27e-5 gradient-L1 reduction; later loss differed by 5.96e-8 and final scalar adapter strength by 5.82e-10. RNG and pretrained weights remained identical/unchanged.
diagnostic_evidence.hypothesis: Concurrent CPU autograd accumulation or reduction scheduling may be causing tiny floating-point differences. This is not yet established as the cause.

change.only_change: Disable CPU autograd engine multithreading during loss.backward() with torch.autograd.set_multithreading_enabled(False).
unchanged: dataset, sequence roles, clips, and frame order
optimizer, learning rate, weight decay, losses, and update schedule
intra-op thread count, device, dtype, and deterministic-algorithm setting
change.reason: Execution scheduling only; the change is intended to make the already-frozen CPU training path exactly repeatable, not to alter the method or improve efficacy.

required_checks.scope: Repeat the exact two-row frozen clip prefix twice from fresh starts for the frame-broadcast arm, then both arms if the isolated control passes.
required_checks.pass: Exact equality of initial adapter, optimizer, and full RNG; per-update receipts and losses; final adapter and optimizer tensor state; and full RNG. No tolerance relaxation is allowed.
required_checks.failure: Keep the full efficacy run stopped and diagnose the remaining first differing value. Do not alter thresholds or comparisons.

interpretation: This amendment resolves only a deterministic-training engineering condition if its exact replay check passes. It is not a research result and does not authorize efficacy training unless the complete real-checkpoint gate passes.
